title: Guyana's Oil Boom: The World's Fastest-Growing Economy Is in the Caribbean | Across the Water, Ep. 1
lede: The IMF projects Guyana's economy will grow 22.3% in 2026, the fastest of any country and more than double the next. Ten years after its first offshore oil discovery, crude now earns more than nine of every ten dollars Guyana makes from exports. This episode explains how the boom works, who it is reaching, and what could go wrong.
keyPoints: The IMF's October 2026 World Economic Outlook projects 22.3% growth for Guyana this year, first in the world; Taiwan is next at 10.7%.
ExxonMobil's Liza-1 well found oil in 2015; production began in December 2019 and passed 900,000 barrels a day by the end of 2025.
Crude exports earned US$15.05 billion in the first half of 2026, about 93% of all export earnings (Mid-Year Report).
Under the 2016 production-sharing agreement, Guyana takes a 2% royalty; companies recover costs from up to 75% of output; remaining profit oil is split 50/50.
The Natural Resource Fund held about US$4.1 billion at the end of April 2026; the IMF says more of any windfall should be saved.
Venezuela claims the Essequibo region, about two-thirds of Guyana's land; the ICJ heard the case in May 2026 and its ruling is pending.
